{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took stroke 3, the upper tail fin, on the pad Hana sketched. I laid it so it picked up as soon as the body reached the crossing, and Jack and Hana both confirmed it was connected through to the tip. That was my one concrete contribution. The plan, the sketch, the body and the lower fin redo came mostly from Hana, Sofia and Jack. I don't have the judge's result in front of me, so I can't claim the fish was recognised. It was a clean fish outline with all 97 dominoes connected to the start.

Execution: My fin went down without needing a redo, and I stayed off the lower fin while Hana relaid it, so we never collided. After the fin was in, I kept my hands off to avoid bumps. That was sensible, but I also never offered to take on anything else, such as a second check of the joints or the loose dominoes by the crossing. I could have done more with the spare time.

Collaboration: I took the assignment quickly, said I was queued on the fin, and didn't pile onto the fin disagreement between Sofia, Jack and Hana. I answered the manager's check-ins with accurate status. Much of my talk, though, was cheering and repeating what others had already said, rather than adding new information.

Leadership: This was not where I added the most. Hana set direction and I followed it well. I helped keep the mood light and the table calm in the last minutes, but I didn't drive decisions or catch problems. Next time I'd put my free hands to use sooner, for example by independently inspecting an area, instead of waiting."}
